projectSummary: This is the only retrieved study that measures the index press and a cable fly-family condition in the same participants with the same instrumentation. It is mechanical, not adaptive: nothing in it measures muscle size or strength change, so it cannot support any hypertrophy statement. The cable cross-over here is a related condition with an unreported pulley height, so it is not a measurement of index Y.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: Shoulder kinematics were simplified to upper arm relative to thorax with no separate clavicle or scapula segment; the authors name this as the key limitation and note that scapular protraction matters at the end of the bench press.
Quasi-static inverse dynamics; loads set as a percentage of body weight rather than of 1RM, so intensity relative to each participant's capacity is unknown and may differ between the exercises.
The cable cross-over setup is under-reported: pulley height, stance and elbow-angle prescription are not stated, which is exactly what the index-Y definition turns on.
No electromyography, so no statement about pectoralis major activation is measured here.

study.intervention: bench press flat; bench press inclined; cable cross-over; cable pull-over
study.population: Twenty healthy participants (10 male, 10 female), age 24.9 (SD 2.7) years, height 175.2 (SD 9.0) cm, mass 68.6 (SD 11.1) kg; inclusion 18-45 years with at least two hours per week of weight training experience; exclusion current injury or illness, previous shoulder or upper-limb surgery, neurological disorder or current medical treatment.

title: Chest Exercises: Movement and Loading of Shoulder, Elbow and Wrist Joints.
